articleTitle: Performance Analysis of 20 Gbps-60 GHz OFDM-RoFSO Transmission with ODSB and OSSB Modulation Using Hybrid Mode
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Radio-over-free-space-optics (RoFSO) technology is used for transmission of millimeter wave signal using optical network without requiring any optical fiber installation. In this work, the transmission of 20 Gbits/s-60 GHz information is carried out through an OFDM system with 512 subcarriers that are multiplexed in a single channel. By using mode combining technique, Laguerre Gaussian (LG) 01 mode and Hermite Gaussian (HG) 00 modes are combined to generate a hybrid mode for signal transmission in FSO environment. A Dual port Dual drive Mach-Zehnder Modulator (DD-MZM) is configured to generate ODSB and OSSB modulated signals at its output. ODSB and OSSB based systems are compared in terms of received power and signal to noise ratio (SNR) at detector output. A similar analysis is done to measure received power and SNR by using 2, 3 and 4 bit QAM encoder. A 60 GHz RF signal is transmitted through an FSO link using hybrid optical mode to investigate performance in mitigating fading effect due to atmospheric turbulence under clear weather condition.

articleTitle: Cervical Cancer Risk Prediction Using XGboost Classifier
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Machine learning is now the most recurrently used computational technique for clinical diagnosis. Many algorithms have been developed for the prediction and identification of various diseases at an early stage, which benefits in decreasing the mortality rate. Several studies indicate that even after the development of a vaccine, cervical cancer remains the prime cause of death in women when compared with other cancer types. Cancer risk predictions have been helpful for targeted screening and maximizing treatment gains. In this paper, a scalable tree boosting method, known as Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) has been used to achieve cervical cancer risk prediction. The tuned model uses regularization and handles missing data with its in-built sparse-aware and quantile algorithms. It also outperforms the available state-of-the-art machine learning models, through its parallel computational capabilities and distribution across clusters. The results enhance the chances of applying machine learning to identify the relevant disease predictors and thus become an important tool for early detection of cervical cancer.

articleTitle: Deep Convolutional Neural Network with ResNet-50 Learning algorithm for Copy-Move Forgery Detection
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: One of the most well-known kind of image forgery is copy-move forgery (CMF). In CMF, one segment of an image is copied and pasted into another segment of an identical image in order to hide crucial data or include new data in the image. For that reason, falsification revealing methods are necessary to recognize altered territories. A new, quick, and capable copy-move forgery detection (CMFD) method is constructed and tested in this study. To classify CMF in a rapid and reliable manner, the proposed method utilizes a Deep Convolutional Neural Network (DCNN) that integrates Residual network framework with 50 layers (ResNet-50). The residual network uses the concept of skip connection which adds the original input to the output of the convolutional layer and will remove the problem of vanishing and exploding gradient that occurs in the traditional Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model. The accuracy and logarithmic loss (LogLoss), which is a function of cross-entropy, have been employed to assess the performance and efficiency of the algorithm. The results are evaluated on the CoMoFoD dataset after dividing it into training and test set. According to the results, the proposed algorithm achieved better accuracy and reduced the LogLoss function at 100 epochs.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of MIMO FSO System and WDM FSO System for Leh (Ladakh), India under Worst Weather Conditions
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Free space optics (FSO) as an optical wireless communication gained great attention to manage the disaster problem by providing license-free highly secure transmission with low-cost deployment and high bandwidth. Besides all these, atmospheric turbulence-induced fading can become a major challenge for FSO systems as it affects their performance. This paper proposed a novel design for multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) FSO and hybrid wavelength division multiplexing (WDM) with multiple beams FSO systems by considering the rain, fog, dry snow, scintillation loss, geometric loss, and Rytov variance over Gamma-Gamma distribution. The results are offered in the form of Bit Error Rate (BER), Quality Factor (QF), and Eye Diagrams.

articleTitle: A Numerical Study of Analog Parameter of Negative Capacitance Field Effect Transistor with Spacer
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: In this work, we studied the negative capacitance field effect transistor with spacer (NCFET(spacer)) for enhanced analog and digital parameters in contrast to the conventional negative capacitance field effect transistor (NCFET) employing a new idea of ferroelectric layer (HfO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>FE). Visual TCAD simulator is applied to model NCFET(spacer). The outcomes have been examined in form of transconductance (G<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</inf>), unity gain cutoff frequency (F<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">t</inf>), intrinsic gain (A<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">v</inf>), leakage current (I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">off</inf> ), Early Voltage (V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ea</inf>), transconductance generation factor (TGF), and NCFET(spacer) upgraded concert of switching ratio I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">on</inf>/I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">off</inf> by 105% over NCFET, output conductance (G<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d</inf>), improved subthreshold swing (SS) by 5.7% over NCFET, lower drain barrier induced lowering (DIBL) by 28% over NCFET. Therefore, NCFET(spacer) can be appropriate for analog and digital circuit analysis.

articleTitle: A Wideband Antipodal Vivaldi Antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: This paper presents the design of a antipodal Vivaldi antenna (AVA) with wideband. The plated through vias (PTH) are incorporated in AVA for performance enhancement. The proposed AVA with vias (AVA-V) is fabricated on Roger’s RO4003 substrate and its size is 45 mm × 20 mm × 0.8 mm. The PTH vias have improved the conventional CAVA peak gain by 11.4 dBi. The AVA is designed to provide a very wide bandwidth of 165.85% and its range is from 4.2 GHz to 45 GHz. Next, the feeding structure of the ground is also changed for further antenna parameter enhancement. The AVA-V results depict that the proposed antenna can be used for various wireless communication applications like ultra-wideband (UWB), 5G technology, radar, Ka-band, and so on.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Assessment of Current Trends in Negative Bias Temperature Instability (NBTI) Deterioration
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: As we move toward ultradeep submicron technology nodes, device aging is getting more severe. The purpose of this article is to provide an in-depth overview of current optimization methods for negative bias temperature instability (NBTI) that are available in the literature. Under the optimization framework, the differences between compensation and mitigation methods have been explored and contrasted with one another. The comprehensive study carried out would offer circuit designers with background recommendations for adopting any method for NBTI aware circuit optimization, regardless of the technique used.

articleTitle: Newly Realized Grounded Capacitance Multiplier Using Single CFDITA
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: This article presents the new realization of capacitance multiplier based on current follower differential input transconductance amplifier (CFDITA). Capacitance multiplier has been realized by one active block CFDITA, three resistors and one capacitor. Multiplication factor of the realized capacitance multiplier can be controlled by using external resistors as well as by bias current of CFDITA. Ideal & non-ideal analyses have been carried out for the implemented circuit. PSPICE software is used for designing & simulation of circuit in 0.18μm CMOS technology. To power the circuit, ±1.25 V is used. The simulation results are found in accordance with theoretical aspects.

articleTitle: IoT Based Smart Indoor Environment Monitoring and Controlling System
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: The population explosion is affecting the air quality adversely, also various kinds of dangerous gases spreads in our environment which are released by the industries and factories etc. causes air pollution. In this study an Internet of Things (IoT) technology based indoor monitoring and controlling device is introduced which greatly help the people life and their works. IoT is the latest or unique technology which connects device to the internet without human interruption. It enables devices to interact, collaborates and learns from each other experiences just like human beings.In the present scenario most of the people spend more than 90% of their time in artificial environment and if any changes in the quality of the environmental conditions occur, it leads to spread out multiple kinds of health problems or diseases which affect the human body for example, cancer, asthma, paralysis etc. To eliminate all these conditions, there is a need of continuous monitoring of indoor air quality which can be achieved by IOT based devices. In the present study, the implementation of an IoT based indoor ambience monitoring and controlling platform is presented to achieve good indoor quality, and it also have benefits such as less costly, less time consuming, more efficient and has been able to achieve paperless workflow in the world of busy environment without involving human to human interaction.

articleTitle: Multi Feedback LFSR Based Watermarking of FSM
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Many techniques are available nowadays, for Intellectual Property(IP) protection of Digital circuits. Out of these techniques, the popular one is watermarking. Similar to the watermarking used in case of text, image and video, watermarking of digital circuits also modifies a digital circuit design in such a way, that only the IP owner of design is able to extract the watermark form the design. In this paper, Multi – Feedback configuration of Linear Feedback Shift Register(LFSR) is used to watermark a FSM based design. This watermarking technique improves the watermark strength of already existing LFSR based watermarking technique. In terms of hardware utilization, it is significantly efficient than some popular watermarking techniques. The proposed technique has been implemented using Verilog HDL in Xilinx ISE and the simulation is done using ModelSim.

articleTitle: GSM Based Smart Energy Meter with Theft Detection and Load Control
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Smart grid is a two-way digital communication which allows monitoring, control, and analysis of energy delivery network. In this paper, a smart energy meter is proposed for overload detection, automatic billing, and theft detection. The integration of the microcontroller and GSM provides the meter reading network. The proposed system can send the information like consumed energy in kWh, produced charge, security services (line Cut/On) through GSM module. The information can be incorporated into existing energy management system situated at power organizations or associations. This project can offer all necessary types of assistance distantly for metering and billing accurately. In addition to that, the power theft in house or in industries can be detected by vibration sensor automatically. The energy theft is an issue that keeps tormenting power usage across country. The goal of this paper is to diminish the unlawful utilization of power and moreover decline the odds of theft.

articleTitle: Network Lifetime Improvement for WSN Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Wireless sensor networks is one of the most competent technology for handling civil and military applications due to the ease of deployment of sensor nodes. At the same time WSN is associated with internal and external factors which demands redesigning of the network. Since WSN is dynamic in nature the self learning Machine learning algorithms can react according to the changing WSN. This paper uses machine learning clustering approach to analyze performance of LEACH protocol in terms of residual energy and network lifetime of Sensor Nodes.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Stack Gate Oxide Underlap TFET Utilising Metal Strip Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: To overcome the performance degradation due to underlap in Stack Gate Oxide Tunnel Field Effect Transistors is the most crucial issue. Thus to ameliorate the performance of stack gate-oxide tunnel field effect transistor with underlap at the gate-source region, implantation of metal strip with low work function in the oxide region is proposed in this work. The simulation graphs show that the stacked device with live metal strip namely Low Work Function Live-Strip-Dual-Material Gate-Oxide-Stack Double-Gate TFET (LWLS-DMGOSDG TFET) performance is better than conventional DMGOSDG TFET with regards to performance parameters such as charge concentration, energy band, transfer characteristics and electric fields. These are the few graphs which proves the applicability of the device with regards to DC electrical Figure of Merits (FoMs). The device simulation has been performed in semiconductor device design simulation tool, 2D-TCAD by Synopsys.

articleTitle: Xplore Word Embedding Using CBOW Model and Skip-Gram Model
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Word embedding has gained a lot of attention in recent years. To learn the systematic relation between words from a large junk of unlabeled text data is quite popular these days while using in Machine Translation, Question Answering or even in Text summarization. Computer understand only 0’s and 1’s now can understand text by simply using word embedding and making vectors in corpus i.e. word vector to represent them in numerical form which are used to perform linear algebra on the words which are now in numerical form in vectors. Word embedding is very effective tool in natural language processing (NLP), both CBOW (Continuous bag of words) and SKIP GRAM have increased the efficiency of word embedding along with it both models have reduced the training time. This paper is divided into two parts. In the first part we have discussed what is word embedding along with two models to implement word embedding, these models are continuous bag of word and skip gram. Our objective is to implement these two-model using shallow neural networks. In second part we have compared the efficiency of both the model while using different size of data sets.

articleTitle: Influence of Nano Ranged Stack Gate on Junctionless Tunnel Field Effect Transistor
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: In the research investigation, we have explored a Dual-Layer (DL) structure on junction-less tunnel FET (JL-TFET) and named as DL-JL-TFET (proposed device). In this approach, the oxide layer is divided into two parts with low-K dielectric materials (SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) and high-K dielectric material (HfO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>). We have introduced Dual-Layer (DL) approach as it offers enhanced capacitive coupling at gate-channel regions plus diminishes tunneling-barrier width near the source-channel region which will upsurge the tunneling current. For better contrast, the DL-JL-TFET and conventional JL-TFET are compared and tentative consequences have shown enhancement in ON current (I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">on</inf>), point subthreshold-slope (Pt. SS) along with analog/RF figure of metrics (FOMs). All these tentative results are obtained with the help of SILVACO ATLAS TCAD software. Additionally, the DL-JL-TFET device oxide thickness has been optimized to choose the better tunneling efficacy. Hence, the DL-JL-TFET device is suitable for low-power and high-speed frequency applications.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of FHSS (Frequency Hopping Spread Spectrum ) Synthesizer
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: This work aims to design and implement a secure frequency hopping spread spectrum system (FHSS) on an FPGA. Design is modelled using the Verilog HDL module. In this work, Xilinx ISE Design suite 14.4 software is used along with the ModelSim simulator and XST synthesizer. The core of the FHSS transmitter is a Direct Digital Synthesizer (DDS) which generate desired frequency signal. This is a very secure communication system because its carrier frequency changes at every fixed interval in a Pseudo-Random manner. In this work, the simulation and synthesis procedure of a frequency hopping binary frequency shift keying (FH/BFSK) spread spectrum system is designed and described.

articleTitle: Emotion Recognition Using Rational Dilation Wavelet Transform For Speech Signal
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Speech based emotion recognition is an emerging area in human computer interaction. It can improve the performance of smart assistant systems. In this work, a wavelet based approach is proposed for the classification of emotions. In proposed method, rational dilation wavelet transform, which has adjustable quality factor and high frequency resolution, is employed. Wavelet based features are extracted and statistically examined by using Kruskal-Wallis test. Further, these features are utilized for training and testing of K-nearest neighbors, ensemble, and decision tree classifiers variants. Among, all the classifiers optimizable ensemble classifier achieves the highest accuracy.

articleTitle: Analysis and Simulation of Multi-Stepped and Multi-Folded Piezoelectric Energy Harvester
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: In recent years, the development in the area of wideband piezoelectric energy harvesters enabled the possibility to scavenge electrical energy from a wide range of vibrational frequencies. In this direction, this paper proposed a multi-stepped and multi-folded structure of piezoelectric energy harvester to efficiently harvest the electrical energy from a wide range of low frequency vibrations. Here, the substrate beam is folded into eight segments and every segment consists of a layer of piezoelectric material. The proposed structure is featured with the advantages of long substrate length, large strain, wide bandwidth and results in appropriate values of voltage and output power response. The finite element analysis (FEA) of proposed structure shows five resonant peaks within 0–300 Hz frequency range with 2.75 V and 3780 μW maximum values of voltage and power response at 80 Hz resonant frequency.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Polar Codes in 5G New Radio
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Polar codes are simple and efficient capacity-achieving channel codes proposed for binary-input discrete memoryless channels. Recently, 5G communication systems have adopted polar code as a channel coding scheme for control channels due to its modest encoding and decoding complexity. To accomplish further research in polar codes, understanding the concept of polar encoder and decoder and analyzing the performance in various channel conditions are very important. This paper is aimed at the performance analysis of non-systematic polar code in the Rayleigh fading channel in terms of bit error rate. The simulation results exhibit the outstanding performance of polar codes in the Rayleigh fading channel.

articleTitle: Impact of Different Technology Node on the Delay and Power Dissipation of 6T SRAM Cell
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: In this paper, the timing performance and power dissipation of 6T static random-access memory (SRAM) cell for different technology nodes are observed, and the impact of varying supply voltage on each technology node is also analyzed. The simulation of the 6T SRAM cell is done using the Pyxis Schematic tool by Mentor Graphics. For this simulation, different technology nodes, i.e., 130nm, 90nm, 65nm, and 45nm BSIM CMOS process, are used. Finally, it summarized the performance of the 6T SRAM cell in terms of propagation delay, power dissipation (static and dynamic power), and power delay product (PDP).

articleTitle: H-Plane Bow-Tie SIW Horn Antenna for K Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Bow-Tie Antenna based on SIW technology is one of the capable candidate for broad range spatial coverage. By utilizing the substrate integrated waveguide technology for making horn antenna is suitable for fabrication on a single PCB at a lower cost. The antenna has an omni-directional radiation pattern with rippled E-plane fields. The antenna achieves a gain of 7.5dBi and radiation efficiency greater than 93%. Antenna is designed in H-plane i.e. perpendicular to the E-field. Automotive radar antenna should be fabricated on tight space and it should have large coverage area. The proposed design provides large space coverage by dual beam on both sides in the end fire direction. The antenna works at 24GHz, which suits for automotive radar applications for short range.

articleTitle: A UHF RFID Reader Antenna Design for Retail Self-Billing Application
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: In this paper an overview of an Ultra High Frequency RFID reader antenna for retail self-billing applications has been discussed. As each application of retail management vary for this region the role of RFID reader becomes important. Here all the requirements for UHF RFID reader and their antenna performance for retail practical application have been analysed and compared with various exiting antenna design. An example of reader antenna at centre frequency 900Mz with 4.5dBi gain is discussed.

articleTitle: Comparison of Agricultural Drones and Challenges in Implementation: A Review
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: The agriculture industry is under incremental transformation with the aim to optimize on resources and maximize on productions to bridge the gap between demand and supply for growing population. Emerging technologies such as Unmanned Aerial Vehicle and Internet of Things (IoT) when equipped with the cameras and sensors have the lot of potential to provide data-driven solutions for precision agriculture. Agriculture has become an obvious target for big data analytics and cloud computing vendors to exploit the value hidden inside the data, and convert the farms into factories by optimizing every step of the agricultural cycle from seedling to harvesting. In this paper, we discuss that how drones can be utilized for agricultural data analysis with IoT. The paper overviews on the supporting technologies such as big data analytics and cloud computing for providing data-based solutions and comparison of agricultural drones. Furthermore, the challenges in the implementation of drone using IoT are also discussed.

articleTitle: An Optimization Technique for Wireless Communication based on Mesh Topology
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) are usually deployed in several specific places to observe or monitor various environmental situations. Sensors have ability to sense, transmit and retransmit (reply) their data to other neighbor nodes through the network or to the base station either directly or through multi-hop. The development of WSN applications was directed to support different activities. Limitations on their sizes, control and costs add many constraints on the network performance such as transmission range, sensing range, coverage area, lifetime, computation and memory. The sensor networks can be used and linked together depending on the mesh topology. This network is called Wireless Mesh Network (WMN). Wireless Mesh (WM) consist of mesh routers, mesh clients, and gateways. The focus in this article is how to evaluate and improve the performance of the WMN by increasing its throughput. In this article a regression model is utilized as a mathematical tool to predict and expect the number of the possible links and their lengths in each suggested network topology. Shortest paths are also estimated and evaluated for different networks.

articleTitle: Separation of Overlapping Chirp Signals Using STFRFT
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: In signal processing, separation of signals overlapped in either time or frequency domain is one of the crucial phenomenon wherever analysis is to be performed on an individual signal. However, neither time domain windowing nor frequency domain filtering is able to separate the signals if they are overlapped in both the domains. This article presents an alternate method using short time fractional Fourier transform (STFRFT) for the separation of chirp signals which have got overlapped in both the domains of time and frequency. Efficacy of the proposed method has been tested on the composite ultrasound signal of an earlier reported work, generated by the addition of three overlapping chirp signals. The simulated results of proposed work demonstrate that all three components of this composite ultrasound signal are separated successfully and recovered with smaller error in comparison to previous work.

articleTitle: Third Order Low Frequency Sinusoidal Oscillators Employing CFOAs and Grounded Capacitors
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: In this communication, two new third order low frequency sinusoidal oscillators (TOLFSO) employing current feedback operational amplifiers (CFOAs) have been presented. The circuits employ four CFOAs, four/five resistors and three grounded capacitors. The proposed circuits offer fully decoupled/ separate control of oscillation condition (OC) and oscillation frequency (OF). To corroborate the theoretical propositions, experimental results have been included using off-the-shelf available CFOA IC AD844.

articleTitle: Moving Horizon Estimation Based Stochastic Filtering of RC Circuit
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: This paper presents output voltage estimation of RC low pass circuit using the moving horizon estimation (MHE) method. For this, we introduced a deterministic state-space model of RC low pass filter (LPF) based on differential calculus. Finally, the MHE method has been used for obtaining optimal output voltage in the presence of noise. We used MATLAB software is to simulate the derived mathematical equations. The estimated outcome is then compared with output obtained from PSPICE simulation when fractional parameter values are varied. Deviation of estimated output is computed in terms of root mean square error (RMSE) to express the loss function.

articleTitle: Electrostatic Analysis of Ferroelectric and High Dielectric Layer Assisted MOSFET
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Report presents a hybrid structure of MOSFET with insulator and the ferroelectric assisted substrate is proposed. The structure has two layers of insulator and one layer of ferroelectric material. The applied gate voltage controls the channel conductivity. The comparison investigation is done for conventional MOSFET and FE-MOSFET structures. In comparison, it is observed that the leakage current for the FE-MOSFET structure is reduced significantly, which leads to a better switching ratio (I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">on</inf>/I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">off</inf>) and reduced subthreshold swing (SS) value, which occurs due to short channel. In addition, the drain induced barrier lowering (DIBL) becomes better in the proposed device structure. The minimum voltage required to turn on the device is also reduced in the case of new proposed architecture of MOSFET. As on state current drive current (I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">on</inf>) of MOSFET, it depends upon the channel electron mobility. Thus, the factors like potential, electric field, electron mobility, and energy bandgap are discussed for both structure. These parameters are carried out by using the Cogenda Visual TCAD tool. It has been observed in simulation that the leakage current is reduced by 97.05%with an increase of 3.60%in on-state drive current for FE-MOSFET structure.

articleTitle: An Autonomous Electronic Zoological Feeder
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Feeding wild animals is a significant issue at zoos, as keepers are required to come into direct contact with wildlife. When their feeding cycle is disrupted, they may become violent in their pursuit of food from zookeepers/people, leading to deadly injuries. Altering animal feeding can also affect animal behavior, causing animals to travel in greater groups to be fed by visitors, increasing the likelihood of disease transmission between animals and assaulting visitors. The paper presents an autonomous zoological feeder system that will find the shortest way feasible to feed the animal while avoiding obstructions. The road route network connecting different animal junctions/caged inside the zoo is described as a matrix with the nodes’ distances as weights. The route network has been mapped to a parameter indicating the obstruction at the identified nodes. The obtained results demonstrate the simulation of an ideal path for the feeder to follow in Proteus that is shorter in distance and free of obstructions, using supporting modules and libraries for the Arduino Nano development board and Bluetooth connectivity.

articleTitle: A Compact Dual-Band Monopole Antenna Loaded with CRLH Unit Cell Exploiting Meandered Line Geometry
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: This paper presents a novel, compact composite right/left handed transmission line based monopole antenna loaded with meander line structure. The proposed antenna is printed on 25 × 25 × 1.6 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> FR4 substrate having dielectric constant of 4.4 + j0.088. To give an insight into working mechanism of the antenna parametric study, electric field distribution and equivalent circuit model have been explained in detail. It is found that the loading of CRLH transmission line leads to miniaturization of the antenna design and miniaturized electrical size of the antenna is calculated as 0.26 λ × 0.26 λ × 0.016 λ, where λ is free-space wavelength corresponding to lowest resonant mode i.e. 3.13 GHz. Measured results show that the suggested antenna exhibits dual-band resonance at 3.09–3.27 GHz (centered at 3.17 GHz) and 4.40–4.50 GHz (centered at 4.47 GHz). A good impedance matching is obtained at both operating bands. It provides simulated peak gain of 1.93 dB and 2.66 dB with corresponding radiation efficiencies of 88.83 % and 78.87 % at 3.13 GHz and 4.49 GHz, respectively. The dipole pattern is obtained in azimuthal plane (H-plane) and omnidirectional pattern is obtained in elevation plane (E-plane). In addition, the presented antenna offers excellent co-to-cross polarization ratio at both the bands.

articleTitle: Conditional Generative Adversarial Network for Devanagari Handwritten Character Generation
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: In the deep learning era, the model requires more variations in the large dataset for better understanding. Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) are often used to learn to generate various images. The design of GAN consists of a collection of neural networks used in an unsupervised way. In GAN, many kinds of arrangements of neural networks are possible for various applications in many areas of computer vision and machine learning. Conditional Generative Adversarial Network (CGAN) is one of them helpful in the generation of the definite type of images. This work illustrates the use of CGAN for generating specific Devanagari handwritten characters.

articleTitle: Underwater Image Enhancement Using Bi- Histogram Equalization with Fuzzy Plateau Limit
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: The images captured in hazy underwater conditions suffer from having poor contrast and low visibility. Hence there is a need for the enhancement of imaging data from underwater exploration and inspection activity so that it can be analysed to extract the desired information. Also, the image enhancement technique must be computationally efficient for it to be used in real time environment. In this paper a novel contrast enhancement technique is proposed called ‘Bi- Histogram Equalization with Fuzzy Plateau Limit’ (BHEFPL) which is an extension to bi-histogram equalization with clipping to be used for underwater image enhancement. The proposed method employs the use of fuzzy logic so as to perform optimal enhancement with respect to image performance metrics which also results in improved visual quality. The proposed technique trumps other contrast enhancement methods in terms of objective and subjective analysis.

articleTitle: Single OTA Based Dual Mode First-Order All-Pass Analog Network
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Operational transconductance amplifier, a resistor and a capacitor are being used in this proposed work to construct a dual mode first-order all-pass analog network. The presented circuit has a distinguishing feature that allows it to operate in both voltage-mode and current-mode. In order to get all-pass filter response in both modes, the circuit does not require any physical alterations. The non-ideal as well as parasitic analyses are also included to evaluate the real time performance of proposed structure. The importance of design has been highlighted by using Monte-Carlo analysis to explore the impacts of capacitor changes as well as the effects of temperature variations. Using ± 1 V power supply and 0.18 μm CMOS process parameters, the theory of the proposed circuit is validated using PSPICE simulation.

articleTitle: Enhancing the Food Image Classification Accuracy Using Ensemble of CNNs and HelperNet
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Image classification is an important research area spanning diverse fields and has evolved finding new applications with the use of deep learning techniques involving convolutional neural networks (CNNs). With the growing penetration of the social media in day-to-day lives, people sharing food images on various platforms has necessitated improved food classification systems. In this work, we use multiple combinations of the food image classification CNNs and improve the classification accuracy for the food images. We propose a multi-layer CNN architecture called the HelperNet, which improves the accuracy of food image classification when combined with the traditional CNNs like AlexNet, GoogLeNet, ShuffleNet, and SqueezeNet. We show through the simulation results that such a combination gives the accuracy value of 95.5%. We extract the features from the traditional CNNs and combine these multiple features to form a significant feature vector to get a better classification accuracy. We also propose image pre-processing, i.e., sharpening the image center and fading the boundaries, further enhancing the image classification accuracy. Further, we also compare the effect of feature extraction from different levels of CNNs. The analysis and numerical results on classification accuracy serve as a useful benchmark in this burgeoning field.

articleTitle: Tunnel Field Effect Transistor Based Biosensors: A Review
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Tunnel field effect transistor (TFET) based biosensors are becoming prominent as a good electronic device for label-free biomolecules detection. This paper presents a review of different structures of the TFET based biosensors. The basic idea behind the concept of label-free detection of biomolecules is the conversion of biological events to the electrical signals. These biological events include the biomolecules, which can be detected by two approaches, namely gating effect and dielectric modulation. Biomolecules are categorized as charged and neutral biomolecules. For the detection of these charged/neutral biomolecules various biosensor structures based on TFET have been adopted. Therefore, this paper provides a brief summary on different TFET based biosensors for label-free detection of biomolecules. This paper also shows that TFETs are found as the promising candidate for biosensor application.

articleTitle: Energy Optimization via Optimal Placement of Cluster Heads in Wireless Sensor Networks with Obstacles
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: In this paper, we present a technique to ensure complete network coverage and minimize the energy consumption in wireless sensor networks (WSNs) that have natural obstacles. These obstacles may prevent data transmission between the components of the network to reach the final destination or the base station (BS). Initially, we split the network into groups and clusters using graph partitioning technique and -mean clustering algorithm, respectively. We assign one cluster head (CH) for each group. Then, the problem turned to determine the optimal position of the CH within its group that provides line-of-sight (LOS) between the transmit-only (TO) sensor nodes and their corresponding cluster head (CH), as well as extending the lifetime of the network by reducing the number of operating TO sensor nodes. The last goal achieved using particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm. Two scenarios are compared to assess the proposed algorithm against another standard algorithm. Simulation results show that the proposed model is superior to the other model by about 6 and 7 times for the first and second scenarios, respectively, in terms of the network lifetime.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Compressive Sensing Methods for Speech Enhancement in Hearing Aid Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Enhancing the speech corrupted by real-world noises is a challenge for hearing aid applications. To address it, various filters have been designed with a goal to improve the quality and intelligibility of speech. Compressing sensing (CS) is found to be a promising technique for enhancing speech in various speech processing applications. However, the suitability of CS is limited for hearing aid applications due to higher reconstruction delay. Towards this end, a machine learning-based optimization to CS has been proposed in this work. The proposed solution is a detailed and comparative analysis of various optimizations to CS against the proposed machine learning-based optimization is presented. The performance is compared in terms of standard speech quality metrics and speech reconstruction time. The machine learning-based optimization to CS reconstruction achieves higher performance in both speech quality metric and speech reconstruction time.

articleTitle: Multispectral Remote Sensing Image Classification Using Modern Machine Intelligence Approach
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Classification of multispectral images is a processing tool used in various applications of remote sensing in natural hazards assessment, agricultural and environmental monitoring to assess and analyze current events so as to avoid damage caused by untimely disasters in nature. Several image classifiers have been presented in the past, some of which are supervised classifiers and some unsupervised ones that have been applied to different remote sensing images to classify them. But the classification accuracy on any of the multispectral images is not good enough to identify the real and correct image classes. Therefore, the real and true classification of multispectral images remains a challenging task even today. To accomplish this challenging task, we have presented a novel machine intelligence approach in this paper. The proposed approach is based on the pixels of multispectral images in which the spectral properties of the image have not been changed. The model consists of a total of five layers consisting of three hidden layers in which seven features vectors are applied to the input layer and all hidden layers are activated with the ReLU function. There are four neurons on the output layer, which is activated with the softmax function. The accuracy of the proposed model was achieved at 99.97% with a 0.9997 Kappa coefficient which is 9.04% higher than the previously proposed models. Due to the good accuracy of this model, it can be used for the accurate assessment of any natural disaster and agricultural health monitoring.

articleTitle: Mathematical and Engineering Solutions Facing COVID-19 Pandemic: A Review
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Corona Virus disease (COVID-19) is a new disease started at December 2019 in Wuhan-China and World Health Organization declared officially that COVID-19 is a pandemic at March 2020, this pandemic is counted as the fifth one from 1918. Such situations push the researchers at every field to give their efforts to help people to get through this pandemic. Doctors, Nurses and other medical specialist start to face this situation using the knowledge they have. Beside them researchers in other fields of knowledge try to give some solutions to help the medical staff in their war against the disease. This paper is a review of the mathematical and engineering solutions that helps to know the behavior of the disease and how it spread and to give some methods to reduce the time of diagnosis the patients.

articleTitle: Beam Steering and Tracking for 5G Mobile Communication Network in mm Wave Frequency Band
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: 5G is expected to support enhanced Mobile broadband (eMBB), massive Machine type communication (mMTC), and ultra-Reliable low latency communication (uRLLC). 5G vision relies on a successful roll out of mm Wave frequency technology. Beam forming technology has been introduced in 5G to compensate path losses due to mm Wave frequencies. Beam forming aims to generate different beams for different User Equipment (UE) using an array of antenna elements at the base station to communicate between different users. The effective beams undergo minimum power loss and interference, and are aimed to direct towards the UE. In this paper the beams were formed and linked to the user by collecting the location coordinates of UE and cross-check the most effective beam for that UE based on the deciding parameters. The handover of UE between base stations has been simulated which involves tracking of the UE by the two base stations in the small cells. The simulation has also been carried out for the case where the height of the user is not fixed.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of Dual Drive Dual Parallel Mach Zehnder Modulator Based Radio Over Fiber link for Wireless Networks
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: In this research paper a method to realize a single side band technique in RoF link is demonstrated. Radio over Fiber (RoF) emerges as a part of optical communication system and it has wide variety of application. In spite of having wide variety of application performance parameter of RoF link is limited by non-linear behavior which degrades modulation performance and enhances inter modulation distortion (IMD). In this research paper third orders inter modulation distortion (IMD3) has taken into consideration and comparison is made in terms of IMD3 component suppression with respect to modulator: Single drive MZM and Dual drive dual parallel Mach zehnder modulator (DPMZM) in RoF link. For simulation of proposed model Optisystem software is used. From simulation outcomes, it is found that IMD3 suppressed more in DPMZM in comparison to the single drive MZM in RoF link.

Author Keywords: Dual drive dual parallel Mach zehnder modulator

articleTitle: Effect of Gate Oxide Material Variability on The Analog Performance of T-Gate GaN-MOS-HEMT with Graded Buffer
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: This paper investigates the effect of gate oxide material variability on the analog performance of the T-gate GaN-MOS-HEMT with AlGaN gradient buffer. The different oxide materials such as HfO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> (hafnium oxide), SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> (silicon oxide), and composite HfO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> are investigated. The DC and analog performance for different gate oxides have been studied by the Atlas-Silvaco simulator. The simulated study confirmed that using the HfO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> as a gate oxide significantly reduced the leakage current, a positive shift of threshold voltage (−1.5V), the higher peak of transconductance (0.11S), transconductance generation factor (75V<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>), early voltage (V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">EA</inf>) and intrinsic gain (A<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">v</inf>) is observed. These tremendous results confirm that the proposed structure is applicable for analog applications.

articleTitle: Enhanced Ultrasound Speckle Reduction technique Using SLIC Segmentation and Method Noise Compensation
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: In this paper, an enhanced ultrasound speckle reduction technique using Simple linear iterative clustering (SLIC) segmentation and method noise compensation technique has been proposed. The noisy image is first sparsely represented in its low frequency components with the SLIC superpixel clustering and reconstruction. Then the high frequency method noise is calculated by the difference of the noisy image and the low frequency reconstructed image. The details in the method image are then utilized to enhance the low frequency reconstructed image. The performance of the proposed technique is tested on synthetic ultrasound images with various noise components of different variance. The experiments show promising results of the proposed algorithm in comparison to other existing methods in terms of PSNR, SSIM, EKI and CC.

articleTitle: Dual Band Microstrip Patch Antenna and its Gain Enhancement for X Band and Ku Band Application Using Metamaterial
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: In this paper an efficient dual band inset fed microstrip patch antenna is presented for X band and Ku band application. The antenna is designed by etching four rectangular complementary split ring resonators in the patch of the conventional microstrip antenna and placing a metamaterial superstrate above the substrate. The superstrate layer made of a 5×5 array of rectangular split ring resonators. The proposed microstrip antenna exhibits a very good performance at both resonant frequencies. Initially a conventional patch antenna is designed to operate at 10 GHz. The proposed antenna is tuned to operate at two resonant frequencies 10 GHz and 15.1 GHz. The proposed antenna is simulated using High Frequency Structure Simulator (HFSS 15:0) that obtains a gain of 8.3067 dB at 10 GHz and 9.6068 dB at 15.1 GHz. The four rectangular CSRR etched in the radiating element (patch) is responsible for the second operating band and the superstrate layer is enhancing the gain of the antenna.

articleTitle: Fractional Order Butterworth Filter Design Using Bit Level Cat Swarm Optimization Technique
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Filters play an important role in communication and computation related systems. The aim of designing a Butterworth filter is to find filter coefficients that satisfy the desired specifications for the practical applications. In this work, an evolutionary optimization based on bit level cat swarm Optimization technique approach is used for designing. The bode response of designed filters have been plotted and compared with ideal response. In addition to this bit level cat swarm optimization technique is also used for designing filters.

articleTitle: Stub-loaded Dual-Band Planar Antenna for 28/38 GHz 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: A stub-loaded dual-band patch antenna design is presented for millimeter-wave 5G applications. Two techniques are integrated to design the antenna: first, an inset-fed rectangular patch is designed and then open-circuit stubs of quarter-wavelength are integrated with the feed line. The inset-fed patch has a frequency band of 38 GHz, whereas the stubs are designed to have a frequency band of 28 GHz. For reduced back radiations, a modified ground plane is utilized. This modification tends to enhanced antenna gain and efficiency, which are noted to be 5.5 dBi and 88%, respectively. For the validation of the proposed design, a prototype is fabricated and tested, and a reasonable agreement is observed between both the simulated and measured results.

articleTitle: IsSwap: Deep Fake Detection
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: In this era of technology the intake of information through digital media has grown exponentially and it has provided people with personal motives to spread falsified information among the masses to create biased opinions and a sense of unrest. The falsified information is provided to the people especially during elections to create political unrest among the masses or simply to spread a rumour. Since most of the information consumed by people is in the form of videos, it has become a great target spot for people with malicious intent. Deep-Fake is an emerging threat to celebrities, political faces and JSON common people. The paper is aimed at overcoming the given challenge by providing a fast and reliable method to determine the authenticity of a given video. We have proposed a model for detecting deep fake videos via XceptionNet and ResNet50 together with multiple hidden layers of neural networks. The results shows that the proposed method outperformed other state-of-the-art methods in terms of precision and recall rate and performed well in predicting whether the video is fake or real.

articleTitle: Design of Buffer Circuit for Global Interconnects Using Adiabatic Dynamic Logic
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: The on-chip global interconnects which are used to provide connection has become a real performance factor due to their extremely narrowed cross-section area and scaling of the device into nanometer technology. As the size of the device reduces, the global interconnect delay increases because of an increase in resistance. Due to reduction in chip size and increase in metal levels in the chip interconnect started to control the electrical characteristics thus, constituting total circuit delay. However, this delay can be reduced using the buffer insertion technique. This paper proposes the design of the Schmitt trigger circuit using the Adiabatic dynamic technique to recover energy consumption in the interconnect circuit. Authors have also simulated interconnect circuits using different buffers and a comparison is done with the proposed ADL Schmitt trigger circuit design. Simulations are carried out in a well-established 45nm/1V CMOS process. It is observed that the overall power for interconnect circuit with the proposed ADL Schmitt trigger as a buffer is 3.20pW which is better in comparison with other circuits.

articleTitle: High Efficiency Broadband Mixed Mode Power Amplifier for Patient Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: In this paper, the wideband operation of mixed mode Class F power amplifier has been presented for biomedical application in patient monitoring. The proposed work involves a reactance compensation technique, which provides a 10 W output power for a frequency range of 0.3–2.4 GHz while achieving efficiency of 66.81–76.82% over 155.55% fractional bandwidth. The large signal gain ranging from 11~13 dB and output power greater than 40 dBm. The PAE ranges from 55 to 72%. Layout of proposed circuit is generated using Modelithics components to verify the circuit implementation.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Different GAN Models: DC-GAN and LS-GAN
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Generative Adversarial Networks (GAN) is an excellent method to generate fake images using the training dataset provided. Generative Adversarial Network consists of two sub-networks that is generator and discriminator networks that compete against each to produce the desired output. Regular GAN is not compatible enough for synthesizing images. However, with the use of CNN models for the sub-networks, it is easier to learn the distribution of training images. We demonstrate the performance of CNN based DC-GAN model. However, it can be noticed that sigmoid based cross entropy loss function results in mode collapse and convergence problems. Hence, we further investigated the research using LS-GAN model which uses least square error loss function. Both the models were trained on the same training datasets. To validate the results, generator & discriminator loss and FID scores were calculated. In this paper, fthe different datasets are used to carry out the experiments. Comparison between DC-GAN and LS-GAN models, the impact of changing hyperparameters and the significance of calculated metrics is illustrated.

articleTitle: A Simulation Based Study and Optimization of CdTe/ZnO/ITO Based Device for Self-Powered Photodetector Perspective
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: In this work, we have studied the effect of the top electrode on the performance of CdTe/ZnO/ITO-based devices for self-powered applications. The device is studied using different top metallic contacts such as Palladium (Pd), Nickel (Ni), Gold (Au), and Platinum (Pt). The performance is analyzed in terms of maximum power generation point, which is 4.98, 6.03, 8.67, and 10.45 mAV/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> for Pd, Ni, Au, and Pt electrode, respectively. Pt electrode with a work function of 5.64 eV outperforms the other electrodes. The self-powered response of the device is analyzed for varying thickness of ZnO from 200 nm to 600 nm, and the optimum result is achieved at 450 nm. The device is further analyzed for Quantum Efficiency measurement, and the peak is obtained around ~350 nm, which matches the absorption spectra of ZnO. The Quantum efficiency measurement shows the viability of the device to be used as a self-powered photodetector detector covering the wide region from UV-A (320 nm) to Near Infrared (700 nm).

articleTitle: Implementation of Dual Tree Complex Wavelet Transform with Mean Energy Features to detect Alzheimer’s Disease
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Alzheimer’s disease is an inveterate neurodegenerative disorder that results to gradual loss of cognitive power and memory. It is a chronic disease that reduces the count of neurons in the brain which may lead to patients’ death in due course of time. To reduce the threat of this disease, it is substantial to detect it at its initial stage. Alzheimer’s Disease introduces the structural atrophies in the brain, causing reduction in grey matter densities, reduction of cortical surface and altering the size, shape, and volume of hippocampus. Magnetic resonance imaging is a non-intrusive neuroanatomical technique that shows inner structural differences with good resolution and contrast. In this paper, Dual Tree Complex Wavelet Transform is used for obtaining the features from Magnetic Resonance Images. This paper presents a novel approach for Alzheimer’s Disease and Normal Control classification using the mean energies of real and imaginary components of complex wavelet coefficients taken individually as features. Experimental results with seven different classifiers show that mean energy obtained from real and imaginary components of complex wavelet co-efficient taken separately as features gives more promising result compared to mean energy of real component of complex wavelet coefficient taken as a whole. Through the proposed approach using Open Access Series of Imaging Studies dataset with k-Nearest Neighbor classifier 97.3% Prediction accuracy is achieved along with 98.2% sensitivity and 96.4% specificity while using the same data set with Cubic Support Vector Machine classifier 97.3% prediction accuracy is achieved with 96% sensitivity and 99% specificity. The proposed approach is simple in comparison to existing complex algorithms still it gives better results with regards to accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity.

articleTitle: Design of All Optical Universal Gates using 2-D Photonic Crystals
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Optical domain is preferred over other conventional networks today because the speed is increased with no interference from electromagnetic signal. Digital gates are used in signal processing of optical network which leads to slowing down of the performance of the circuit as there is a need for electro-optic conversion. Hence the implementation of universal gates completely on optical module using 2D-photonic crystal will improve the performance of the optical network. NAND & NOR gates are designed and in use here through the use of 2D-photonic crystals. All other basic logic gates can be implemented by the use of the universal gate. This paper shows the composition of optical-gates (NAND &NOR) on 2D-photonic crystals. The designing of the gates is done in OptiFDDT software. Contrast ratio is obtained to be 18.66dB dB 16.64 in NAND gate and NOR gate respectively.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Novel Heterojunction ESDG-TFET for Analogue/RF Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: In this article performance analysis of Heterojunction Extended Source Double Gate Tunnel Field Effect Transistor (ESDG-TFET) has been done, which is based on the concept of bandgap engineering for RF/analogue applications. The study has been conducted on interfacing of III-V group material along with IV group material, to enhance I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ON</inf> (ON-state current) of the proposed device. It has been shown from the simulations that the proposed device exhibits improved I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ON</inf> (in the order of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−5</sup> A/μm), I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ON</inf>/I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">OFF</inf> ratio (in the order of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</sup>) at V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">DS</inf>=2V. Besides, enhanced transconductance and other RF performance parameters have been obtained for proposed device, which proves the device suitability for various analogue/RF applications. Apart from that, figure of merits of linear distortion like transconductance coefficients, second order voltage intercept point (VIP<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>), third order voltage intercept point (VIP<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>), 1 dB compression point etc. have also been analyzed in detail.

articleTitle: Face Recognition Using Local Multiple Zig-Zag Structure Pattern
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: This paper presents a novel algorithm local multiple zig-zag structure pattern (LMZSP) for face recognition. The proposed method modifies the Weber’s ratio and obtains the local multiple pattern (LMP) images by exploring the relationship between center and neighboring pixels. In order to make these patterns more robust to noise and intensity variations, local multiple zig-zag structure pattern (LMZSP) has been proposed by applying the local zig-zag graph structure (LZGS) on the four LMP images. Further, the resulting high dimensional feature vector is converted to low dimensional feature using linear discriminant analysis (LDA) algorithm. The robustness of feature is tested and analyzed on faces from uncontrolled environment. The recognition results clearly proves the effectiveness of the proposed method as compared to the other state-of-the-art approaches.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of Fibonacci Polynomial Based Power Allocation Algorithm for NOMA in VLC System
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: In this paper, we present an empirical method of power allocation in Non-Orthogonal Multiple Access (NOMA) based Visible Light Communication (VLC) system. A Fibonacci polynomial based power allocation is proposed for allocating power to multiple users in a VLC environment and it’s performance is evaluated in terms of sum rate for different levels of transmit power. Sum rate for four users has been presented in this manuscript. Also, we present the sum rate for different values of semi-angle of LED and Field of View (FOV) of photo detector. It is shown that this method achieves optimum performance.

articleTitle: Single OTRA-Based Multifunctional Filter Configuration
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: This paper presents a new single-input single-output (SISO) type voltage mode filter configuration that employ single operational transresistance amplifier (OTRA) and four admittances. The proposed configuration is capable of realizing second order low pass filter (LPF), high pass filter (HPF) and band pass filter (BPF) using different choices of branch admittances. The proposed filter responses have been verified through PSPICE simulations using CMOS OTRA implemented in 0.18μm TSMC technology and also validated using MATLAB evaluations.

articleTitle: Photonic Crystal Cavity Optimization Using AI
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: In this manuscript, photonic crystal cavity optimization using artificial intelligence has been done. The proposed structure is very simple and has high sensitivity. Porosity in the layers has been intentionally added for ease of analyte infiltrate, which will increase the sensitivity of the crystal but reduces the strength of the transmitted signal. The structure is designed considering alternate layers of high and low refractive index material. For this, SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> and MgF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> materials are considered. The mean error is minimized by considering optimum value of ‘k’ as 4. Different algorithms were checked on the dataset and finally the kNN algorithm has been applied on the dataset and F1-score of about 0.97 is obtained.

articleTitle: Thinned Planar Antenna Array Synthesis: A Multiobjective Improved Binary Cat Swarm Optimization Approach
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: A new algorithm for the synthesis of thinned antenna arrays is proposed in this paper. The synthesis of an antenna array is a cumbersome process involving the optimization of multiple contradicting parameters. These parameters include number of elements in operation, first null beam width (FNBW) and peak side lobe level (PSLL). In this research a new algorithm called multiobjective modified binary cat swarm optimization is introduced. The output of this process gives a pareto optimal front with all the possible designs. A planar antenna array with 10 × 20 array elements was synthesized. The PSLL was reduced to a notable extent when compared to other algorithms with minimum number of active elements.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Area-Power Efficient Generic Modular Adder using Flagged Prefix Addition Approach
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Modular adders are employed in the implementation of multipliers, reverse converters, digital signal processors, cryptography and other various residue number system applications. This paper proposes novel adder architecture for moduli of the form 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup>-K where K is any integer in the range of 3 ≤ K ≤ 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup>-1. The Proposed architecture uses Sklansky parallel prefix adder (PPA) in the first stage adder along with the flagged prefix addition technique in the second stage. Use of flagged prefix addition approach significantly reduces the area and power dissipation when compared with published work. Synthesis is done using 90 nm SAED generic library on Synopsys Design Compiler tool and VHDL is used to model the structures under investigation over an input bit range of 7 ≤ n ≤ 15. Reduction up to 42.5% is obtained in the area-power product of the proposed modular adder structure when compared to earlier presented work.

articleTitle: Static Performance Assessment of Junctionless Accumulation Mode Gate Stack Gate All Around (JAM-GS-GAA) FinFET Under Severe Temperature
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: This paper evaluates the static performance of Junctionless Accumulation Mode Gate Stack Gate All Around (JAM-GS-GAA) FinFET under extreme temperatures. The simulated results of JAM-GS-GAA FinFET reveal an 8.22% increase in the drain current and a 20.58% rise in the transconductance compared to the conventional JAM FinFET. The proposed device shows Zero Temperature Coefficient (ZTC) bias point at 0.725 V gate voltage, i.e., the bias point at which the drain current is not affected by the temperature. A reduction in the quality factor, transconductance, and drain current is witnessed with the surge in temperature. Further, temperature influence on several static parameters like electron concentration, electron mobility, total current density, electron velocity, and band energy are explored. It is noticed that with the temperature rise from 300 K to 500 K, the JAM-GS-GAA FinFET static performance degrades.

articleTitle: Learn By Share (LBS) – An Effective Handoff Algorithm for IEEE 802.11
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Need of channel transformation arises as a mobile node moves from the range of one access point (AP) to the range of another access point. The process of transforming an active session from one channel to another channel of another cell is known as Handoff. In cellular telephony, the network is organized in such a way that it allows seamless Handoff. During seamless handoff, the user does not feel any service breakage. Seamless handoff, also known as soft Handoff, is possible in cellular telephony networks due to the availability of centralized controller and the interface between networks of different service providers. Opposite to cellular telephony networks, WiFi networks are operative in a small range. The WiFi network in the neighborhood of a mobile node may have centralized or decentralized controllers with or without any interface between them. This results in handoff with service breakage. This service break is large enough to degrade the quality of video and other services. This paper proposes a new algorithm known as Learn by Share (LBS). Old algorithm requires new resources in the form of Bandwidth, Channel or Time whereas LBS algorithm proposed in this paper uses already available data and resource. Thus LBS reduces handoff delay by optimized use of Network resources.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Dual Link RF and RF - FSO Transmission System
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: The performance of a dual-link transmission system has been studied in this paper. The first path has a direct radio frequency (RF) link, whereas the second path has an identical and independent link of dual hop decode-and-forward (DF) based RF-free space optics (FSO) cooperative network. Rayleigh distribution is used to represent RF channels, whereas Gamma-Gamma (GG) distribution is used to represent FSO channel. The impact of maximal ratio combining (MRC) diversity strategy on system performance is explored. To analyse the network, unified closed form expressions for outage probability (OP), and average bit error rate (ABER) are obtained in the form of Meijers-G function. Furthermore, novel expression for average channel capacity containing bivariate fox-H function is derived. In addition, the impact of turbulence severity, FSO detection algorithms, and the consequences of pointing error on system performance are investigated. Moreover to have more insight of system performance analytical results are validated by high signal to noise radio (SNR) asymptotic results.

articleTitle: Light Dependency of Modified Source FDSOI based Photo-detector
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: This article presents electrical performance as well as light dependency of proposed modified source FDSOI based photo-detector. In this proposed device a diode is co-integrated under the buried oxide (BOX). The electrical performance dependency of proposed device on back-biasing is firstly evaluated. After investigation of electrical performance of proposed device this back biasing is utilizing to evaluate photo-sensitivity of proposed device. The photo-generated charge carriers get modulated by this back biasing and causes light induced voltage shift by means of capacitive coupling, without direct connection between diode and FDSOI transistor. The simulations are supported by TCAD simulator and suggested that a co-integration of diode with modified source FDSOI based devices are useful for efficient photo-detector.

articleTitle: Design of Low Cost Substrate Integrated E-plane Waveguide Filter for C-band Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: In this article, an E-plane bandpass filter (BPF) based upon substrate integrated E-plane waveguide (SIEW) is presented. Metal strip insertions into the middle layer of the SIEW structure constitute a novel E-plane BPF. A Jerusalem cross defected ground structure (DGS) is introduced into the ground layer to enhance filter bandwidth by shifting the passband and stopband. Further, two more rows of via holes were inserted for the betterment of filter performance. The filter is designed on Fr4 having a dielectric constant of 4.4. The final design of the filter achieves a 3 dB fractional bandwidth of 52.71%, return loss around −30 dB, and an almost 0 dB insertion loss in the passband.

articleTitle: Prototype Development for IOT Based Contactless Heart-rate and Body Temperature Monitoring System
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: Heart diseases cause millions of deaths worldwide. Although there has been a lot advancement in medical science, the quality of health care in remote areas is challenging. Technological advances in the field of communication and medical technology can help in providing quick and efficient health care at reduced cost. This work is based on patient monitoring by a physician without coming in contact with that patient. A kit has been prepared for the patients with the help of internet of things. With the help of this kit, the patient’s heart rate can be monitored by a doctor or a care taker without coming in direct contact with the patient. The kit is a portable device. In addition to this, results are available to take immediate medical attention in the event of an emergency or caregiver and may take required steps for saving the patient’s life. The pulse rate of patient is also available on mobile phone of the physicians which protects them from direct contact with patients and prevents spread of corona. The kit operates using a pulse rate sensor, DHT11 Temperature and Humidity sensor, ESP8266 NodeMCU micro-controller.

articleTitle: Smart Footsteps Power Generation System
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
abstract: The demand for electrical energy is expected to rise steadily in near future. Contemporary methods of generating electrical power are harmful to the environment. Footstep power generation is one of the sustainable electric energy generation technique which is environment friendly. India can exploit it’s large population, to generate footstep power to satisfy the growing demand for electricity. This paper has proposed a smart footstep power generation system which apart from generating and storing electric energy, provides the facility of remote monitoring and controlling. ANN is used to detect the sensor location which is faulty. The system is able to charge a 12V lead battery completely within 10 minutes using a single person (weighing 45 kg) footstep. This battery then further drives two loads – a DC fan and LED for approximately 30 minutes. Charging voltage can be easily scaled up by increasing the number of piezoelectric sensors. An Android mobile app has been developed to monitor and control the system remotely. The ANN is able to detect location of the faulty sensor with 74% accuracy. At the outset, developing a sustainable electricity generating system with smart capabilities is a substantial contribution of this paper.

articleTitle: III-V / Si Heterojunction based Dual Material Stack Gate Oxide TFETs for Low Power Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Signal Processing and Communication (ICSC)
